To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA-binding domain of the transcriptional regulator OmpR is structurally similar to the winged helix domain found in other DNA-binding proteins and that this similarity extends to a common mechanism for DNA-binding.

(1) the DNA-binding domain of the winged helix protein OmpR is a dimer, (2) OmpR binds to DNA as an asymmetric heterodimer, (3) the DNA-binding domains of OmpR and the related winged helix factor H-NS are structurally very similar and (4) the DNA-binding surface is highly conserved between these two proteins.
the DNA-binding domain of the OmpR protein from Salmonella typhimurium has a winged helical fold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which the OmpR protein of E. coli regulates gene expression.
the structural and functional characterization of the DNA-binding domain of the Escherichia coli two-component response regulator, OmpR, and its interaction with DNA.
the structure and function of the OmpR protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA-binding domain of the winged helix family of transcription factors, as exemplified by the crystal structure of OmpR, has a novel fold.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to determine the structures of OmpR in its unphosphorylated and phosphorylated forms and that we were able, for the first time, to show that the phosphorylation of the protein leads to an altered conformation of the DNA-binding domain.
we have determined crystal structures of the winged helix DNA-binding domain of the Escherichia coli transcription factor OmpR in its apo form and bound to DNA.
we are interested in the structure and mechanism of DNA binding proteins, especially those involved in transcriptional regulation.

OmpR is a very interesting protein.
